BACKPORT: media: staging/intel-ipu3: parameter buffer refactoring Current ImgU driver processes and releases the parameter buffer immediately after queued from user. This does not align with other image buffers which are grouped in sets and used for the same frame. If user queues multiple parameter buffers continuously, only the last one will take effect. To make consistent buffers usage, this patch changes the parameter buffer handling and group parameter buffer with other image buffers for each frame. Each time driver will queue one more group of buffers when previous frame processed and buffers consumed by css. Signed-off-by: Tianshu Qiu <tian.shu.qiu@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Bingbu Cao <bingbu.cao@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+samsung@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 8ecc7c9da013e702aa889002e1288521d7533293 git://linuxtv.org/media_tree.git master) BUG=b:139647343 TEST=Sanity checked basic camera functions. Change-Id: I3ad40122f680aac814d5b7a4acbdabd06e2c2edc Signed-off-by: Bingbu Cao <bingbu.cao@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Tianshu Qiu <tian.shu.qiu@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1390163 Commit-Ready: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org>

u2fd: Always enable user keys This change deprecates the "legacy" code path, and enables legacy fallback if users have not swiched explicitly to the new code path. This is a forced migration to the new code path, while still supporting legacy key handles for authentication. For a user who has previously enabled U2F with 'u2f' or 'g2f' mode (but not switched to user keys), this change will cause new registrations to be user-specific, but old keys can still be used to authenticate. No user action is required for this behavior. chaps: Use crypto::ScopedEVP_MD_CTX OpenSSL 1.1 will use _new()/_free() semantics for all CTX types. 1.0 already does so for EVP_MD_CTX, so we can do the switch now, and, while we are at it, use the recommended _ex() forms for Init and Final. Furthermore, let's used the Scoped* version for better pointer lifetime tracking. Since we are just storing a unique_ptr in the struct, we can now pull it out of the union without bloating the struct size significantly. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:738288 TEST=FEATURES=test emerge-sarien chaps Change-Id: I497fa694a406b744d31af944c128192a5888092c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1757197 Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org>

mount-encrypted: add the new cmdline option "insecure" mount-encrypted doesn't store an insecure system key in NVRAM, which allows us to keep encstateful not wiped over TPM clearing and avoids potential unexpected behavior caused by soft-clearing TPM 2.0. The option should only be enabled for testing purposes and will be used in the autotest env. This CL provdes an alternative and simpler way to solve the soft-clearing TPM 2.0 problem mentioned above, compared with the original solution in CL:1753389. BUG=b:139399088 TEST=tested along with CL:1763468: On a chell, make sure the changes are no-op in any case. On a soraka, create the magic file in /mnt/stateful_partition, then 1. Run crossystem to clear the TPM, reboot, and log in. Then, repeat those 3 steps a few times and make sure each time the encrypted partition is not wiped. Also, check if mount-encrypted.log says it uses an insecure system key. 2. Run tpm_softclear to soft-clear the TPM, then run tpm_manager_client take_ownership to re-own the TPM, then reboot. Make sure the encrypted partition isn't wiped and mount-encrypted.log says it uses an insecure system key. 3. Remove the magic file, run crossystem to clear the TPM, reboot, and make sure the encrypted partition is wiped and mount-encrypted.log says it creates a random key and stores it in NVRAM. Change-Id: I68c762de6115ec33e3ea7ebc35f50f7264578b21 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1763467 Tested-by: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Wei-Cheng Xiao <garryxiao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org>
